title: netctl: unexpected authentication state: alg 57980 (expected 0) tra...
body: I use (or have been using) `netctl` to manage internet connections. Sometimes I have problems with name resolution, but usually that's all. I was lazy and did not update Arch for a while, so I got a lot of updates last night. After rebooting, I can't get an internet connection (at least wifi) with `netctl`, though I can connect manually with `ip`, `wpa_supplicant` and `dhcpd`. I have not touched the `netctl` configuration files and I'm trying to connect to a wifi LAN I control, so I know that hasn't changed either. Since I can bring up a connection manually, it doesn't look like hardware, so I'm guessing the problem is something to do with `netctl` itself. I had some difficulty stopping `netctl` to setup the manual connection, because `systemd` `.slice`s remained even after `stop`ping the services. I don't remember seeing these before, but perhaps I just failed to look. In the journal these appear early Hyd 04 21:01:52 mycomputer systemd[1]: Created slice Slice /system/netctl-auto. Hyd 04 21:01:52 mycomputer systemd[1]: Created slice Slice /system/netctl-ifplugd. But I doubt that is relevant. The most relevant line in the journal may be Hyd 04 21:46:40 mycomputer kernel: wlan0: 04:95:e6:63:96:91 unexpected authentication state: alg 57980 (expected 0) transact 2 (expected 2) but I am not really sure I even understand the sequence since I seem to authenticate OK during startup, but with name resolution failing. Then later when I try to restart `netctl`, authentication fails. So, rather than guess what is relevant, I posted the journal to https://paste.c-net.org/WelcomeApproval . Non-working `netctl` config in `/etc/netctl/networkdienw`: Description='networkdienw' Interface=wlan0 Connection=wireless Security=wpa IP=dhcp ESSID='networkdienw' Key=\"XXX Working `wpa_supplicant.conf`: network={ ssid="networkdienw" #psk="pppp" psk=XXX } PS Despite having just logged in, when I try to submit, I'm told I'm not logged in ...
